title: Staged-orchestrator A/B: automated batching + cache-hinting recommendation experiment and rollback automation
creator: Diego Ramos
description: Run a controlled experiment that compares the new staged-orchestrator recommendation engine (automatically selecting batching and cache-hinting configs) against baseline static configs. The goal is to validate end-to-end economics (cost per 1k tokens), latency SLOs, and output quality stability, while exercising an automated safe-apply and rollback mechanism driven by multi-signal telemetry.
experiment_design: Two-arm randomized A/B with per-route bucketing: 10% control (current best static config), 10% treatment (orchestrator recommendations), rest ramped or held as shadow. Allocation per route to ensure minimum exposures: 5000 requests/route in each arm. Run duration: 14 days or until pre-specified stopping criteria. Use stratified sampling across latency-sensitive vs throughput-heavy routes. Instrument counterfactual replay for a subset of live traffic to validate decision surface offline.
statistical_tests: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across multiple metrics
minimum detectable uplift thresholds per metric
success_criteria: no significant increase in hallucination_rate (95% CI)
no customer-facing errors or >0.1% increase in abort_rate
dashboard_requirements: real-time experiment overview with arm-level KPIs and control charts
per-route slice view (latency/cost/quality) with heatmap of effect sizes
alerting thresholds wired to Slack and PagerDuty for latency or quality regressions
statistical summary panel (posterior distributions, credible intervals, MDE)
rollout_plan: If treatment passes success criteria for 48h stability after minimum exposure, staged rollout will auto-promote in 3 steps: 10% -> 40% -> 100% over 72 hours. Promotion requires green signals on cost, latency, and quality panels. Each promotion includes a monitoring hold of 30 minutes with expedited rollback capability.
rollback_plan: Automated rollback triggered on any of: 1) p95_latency increase >5% sustained for 10m, 2) cost spike >25% compared to control baseline in a 5m window, 3) human-labeled quality regression flagged by sampling pipeline. Rollback orchestration uses canary reverse traffic shift to control arm and posts an incident with root-cause prompt set. Post-rollback, run a diagnostic traffic replay and open follow-up ticket to capture fix and re-run experiment.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment configuration checked into infra repo and reviewed (PR: linked)
Dashboards and alerting panels deployed to staging and smoke-tested
Minimum exposures reached per-route and experiment run completes without infra incidents
Automated rollback successfully triggered in simulated failure during smoke stage
notes: Design trade-offs: we prioritize end-user latency and quality over marginal cost savings. For high-sensitivity routes, orchestrator will fall back to conservative config with higher SLAs. We will record full KV cache hit traces for 1% of treatment traffic to diagnose mispredictions. Follow-ups include build a small ML model to predict safe batching window per route.
runbook: Pre-launch: run smoke on staging, validate telemetry pipeline, pre-register alerting channels. During-run: watch experiment dashboard for first 4 hours, escalation path to SRE on-call. Post-run: generate automated report summarizing posterior distributions, effect sizes, and recommendation for productization or rollback.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: hidden quality regressions not captured by automated metrics. Mitigation: conservative human sampling cohort and increased labeling cadence for first 72h. Risk: confounding traffic shifts during holiday events. Mitigation: block experiments during major traffic anomalies and use traffic-stability gate.
next_steps: 1) finalize PRD and get PM sign-off, 2) implement orchestration hooks and automated rollback lambdas, 3) build dashboards and smoke tests, 4) run 72h internal canary against synthetic workloads, 5) launch public A/B if canary green.
communication_plan: Notify platform and product channels 48h before launch, post daily updates during experiment run in #infra-experiments, publish summary to Confluence and tag stakeholders after completion.
